summary: Bratindra Nath Mukherjee was an Indologist and archaeologist. He studied at the University of Calcutta, SOAS (under Arthur Llewellyn Basham), and Cambridge (under Harold Walter Bailey). He served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at Calcutta (1975–1998).

Brendan Ozawa-de Silva works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned doctorates from the University of Oxford (1998–2003) and Emory University (2007–2015). He was an Associate Professor at Life University (2012–2017) and joined Emory in 2022.

Brendan S. Gillon specializes in linguistics, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1976–1985) and served as an Associate Professor of Linguistics at McGill University (~1992–2022).

Bret W. Davis works in philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Vanderbilt University and Kyoto University. His academic career includes posts at Shiga University, Kwansei Gakuin University, Kyoto University, Otani University, and Loyola University Maryland (attested 2007, 2018).
Brian Bocking is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Leeds (attested 1984), where he studied under Michael Pye.
Brian Cutillo worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1963–1967) and later studied under Geshe Wangyal (~1970–1983).

Brian D. Ruppert is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied under Willis Stoesz (~1980–1984). He held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1999–2018) and Bates College (~2018).

Brian Daizen Victoria specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history. He studied at Nebraska Wesleyan, Eihei-ji, Komazawa, and Temple University. He held posts at Auckland, Adelaide, Antioch (2005–2013), and the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies (2013–2018).

Brian Gregory Baumann specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington under György Kara (-2005) and has taught Mongolian at UC Berkeley and the Numata Center (attested 2026).

Brian Houghton Hodgson was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at East India Company College and Fort William College, and served as Assistant Resident and later British Resident at the Court of Nepal (~1820–1843).

Brian J. Nichols works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He studied at the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies and earned his PhD at Rice University (attested 2011) under the supervision of Anne Carolyn Klein.

Bridget Allchin was an archaeologist and Indologist. She studied at the University of Cape Town and earned her PhD at University College London (1950). She was a Fellow of Wolfson College, Cambridge (~1977–2017), and co-founded EASAS and AIIT.
Brigitte Marschall studied at the University of Vienna (~1977–1982), where she earned her doctorate. She later held a post there as an extraordinary university professor (~2000).
Brigitte Steinmann works in Tibetology. She studied under Alexander W. Macdonald and traditional teacher Bahadur Singh, and held a post at the University of Montpellier (attested 2004).

Brij Kishor Tripathi works in Indology and Tibetology. He worked at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1995) and held mathematics teaching posts at KNIT, CIPET, Lukhdhirji Engineering College, and L.D. College of Engineering (2018).

Bronislav Ivanovič Kuznecov was a Tibetologist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1951–1956) under Vladimir Svjatoslavovič Vorob’ëv-Desjatovskij and Boris Ivanovich Pankratov. He also taught there in 1959.

Bronisław Malinowski studied at Jagiellonian University, Leipzig (under Wilhelm Wundt), and LSE (under Charles Gabriel Seligman and Edvard Westermarck). He held a chair in anthropology at LSE (1922–1938) and later served as professor at Yale (~1939–1942).

Bronwyn Finnigan specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied at Melbourne, Sydney, and Auckland (PhD under Rosalind Hursthouse and John Bishop). She held posts at Marquette University (2012–2014) and the Australian National University (2014).

Brook Ziporyn specializes in sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Chicago and Michigan (PhD ~1989–1996). He held faculty posts at Northwestern (~1999–2012) and the University of Chicago, serving as Mircea Eliade Professor (~2016).

Brooke Foss Westcott was a religious studies scholar. He was educated at King Edward's School, Birmingham, and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1844–1848), later holding a post at the University of Cambridge (~1870–1890).
